title: Early look at my top down zombie game, there is a lot of work left!
author: Ill-Range-4954
selftext:
I made this in about 2 weeks with Opus 5.5. It is far from finished, I am not sure how long this will take, but with every new feature and mechanic, there are 10 bugs and other smaller features and mechanic which need fixing/implementing. But it does work in the long run, even if it seems like a nightmare in the short run.  
  
The idea is this: top down, open world, zombie survival, factions, base building, resource management, human vs human battles too, large scale whatever game. Oh and it also needs a story, a lore and missions. And probably other things, some of which I probably noted in somewhere on my phone. It's an ambitious game and I could never do it without help from someone, or in this case, something else. But now I think I have a chance to do it.

And I need to constantly think about the whole thing and ponder how to proceed. However the workflow has been generally okay and I've had my rage moments because of how AI works, but it was okay.

Do you like it?

comments.author: Early_Flamingo5337
comments.body: No offense but, isn't it just project zomboid but 2d?

replies.author: Ill-Range-4954
replies.body: The map design was inspired by zomboid, but the overall gameplay feels more like kenshi combined with rimworld to me, or any similar strategy game. You control multiple people, you build structures, you interact with other npc factions just like in any strategy game, its different than zomboid in that respect. Here you have a whole faction to your control in a sense, not just one character.

replies.author: Early_Flamingo5337
replies.body: That sound better although I'm not very into zombie games I think people may like it

comments.author: Thin-Regular-8807
comments.body: Considering project zombioid been in dev for a decade id say u don't even know how much there yet to do

replies.author: Ill-Range-4954
replies.body: Of course. I am not rushing anywhere with this game.

replies.author: Thin-Regular-8807
replies.body: I like the perspective tho the size of things , top down gory games

comments.author: Moistjamu
comments.body: I love it, you're building one of my dream games

comments.author: InvestigatorHefty799
comments.body: Neat project and looks fun to play. I get you likely did this for gameplay reasons but the line of sight in real life is much farther than a few houses

replies.author: Ill-Range-4954
replies.body: Good point. I might adjust that.

comments.author: FinalTap
comments.body: Out of curiosity  - are you building this on a subscription plan or via API? What plan/costs have you incurred till now?

replies.author: Ill-Range-4954
replies.body: I am using a 100$ monthly subscription and this is my first month doing this.

replies.author: FinalTap
replies.body: That's interesting. So I am presuming this is taking a lot of of those daily / weekly quotas?

replies.author: Ill-Range-4954
replies.body: Yes quite a bit, especially when it makes a mistake or I change my mind, then you have to fix that and everything costs. Or if you tell it to study stuff on the internet for the game, it can send agents which cost a lot. Or it can send agents to check the code. That’s the reason I might take a break for a month or more.

replies.author: FinalTap
replies.body:
Got that.  All the best with completing this, it's pretty awesome.   
  
Who thought we would be able to do this one day firing off prompts :)
